sections.title: Moving the stressed piece to the front
sections.content: In normal order the subject comes first: *La intervención del mediador fue crucial*. To stress the quality, move it to the front. The subject then usually moves behind the verb: *Crucial fue la intervención del mediador*. You know *ser* from A1 Unit 1 and *resultar* from B1 Unit 15, both followed by an adjective; fronting only changes where the words stand. English does the same in formal writing ('Crucial was the mediator's intervention').

sections.title: What can go first
rows: Spotlights a quality: 'Incalculable fue el daño sufrido'
Place or time phrase + verb + subject
Spotlights the setting: 'En aquella ciudad comenzó la rebelión'
Spotlights a quality of the subject: 'De gran importancia fueron los hallazgos'

sections.title: Two rules to keep
sections.content: The verb and the adjective agree with the subject that comes after them: *Decisiva fue la intervención*, *Decisivos fueron los resultados*, *Decisivas fueron las pruebas* (not *fue las pruebas*). And the subject stays behind the verb: *Decisiva la intervención fue* sounds unnatural.

items.spanish: Primordial resultó el acuerdo firmado entre ambos países.
items.english: The agreement signed between both countries turned out to be paramount.

items.spanish: Bajo esa premisa trabajaron los investigadores durante años.
items.english: Under that premise the researchers worked for years.

items.spanish: De enorme relevancia son los hallazgos recientes.
items.english: Of immense relevance are the recent findings.

items.spanish: Insólito resultó el giro político en aquella región.
items.english: Unusual was the political turn in that region.

items.spanish: En aquella ciudad comenzó la rebelión.
items.english: In that city the rebellion began.

sections.content: Fronting works as a climax: use it once in a paragraph, at the moment you want to stress. If every sentence starts with its adjective, the text sounds heavy and artificial.
